messages:

Subject: Security exhibit — clarification on evidence cadence and pen-test window

Neha,

Thanks for sending the draft exhibit. A couple of questions from our security team as we prep the procurement packet:

- Can you confirm the cadence you expect for evidence delivery (SOC 2 reports, configuration snapshots, sample logs)? We need to map supplier evidence to internal audit windows.
- For the penetration test language: do you permit timed access for a customer-run test, or do you restrict to supplier-managed tests? If supplier-managed, what is the proposed window and expected artifacts?
- We’d like to avoid full-system inspection; is a scoped sampling approach acceptable (specific clusters, tagged resources)?

I’m attaching our internal checklist — would prefer to align on cadence and scope before legal finalizes redlines. Also copying Rajiv (security ops).

Regards,
Sarah Jensen
Head of Security Operations
MedTechCo

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — clarification on evidence cadence and pen-test window

Hi Sarah — thanks, and good questions. High level proposal below; happy to walk through on a quick call.

Proposed evidence cadence (three-tier "sampling bands"):

1) Light (quarterly) — SOC 2 Type II, a 30-day configuration snapshot, and an access list export. Low operational footprint; used for ongoing compliance checks.
2) Scoped sample (on-request / triggered) — a 7-day window focused on tagged production clusters (customer-owned account tags). We provide exports (read-only) of the targeted resources and a small sample of logs (rotated & redacted for PII).
3) Full inspection (limited) — supplier-coordinated window (up to 14 days) for deeper forensics or agreed pen-tests; access is strictly read-only, timed, and audited. Any write or privileged activity is not permitted.

Pen test options:
- Customer-run: not permitted against shared production environments.
- Supplier-managed: we can schedule a supplier-supervised pen test on segregated infra (staging) or a timeboxed supplier-coordinated window on production with strict guardrails and an agreed scope.

Scope guidance: we strongly prefer scoping by resource tags and service families (compute, inference runtime, storage) rather than full clusters. This avoids unnecessary exposure.

Next steps: I’ve attached a draft exhibit (Security_Exhibit_v0.9.docx) with these options. If this aligns, propose a 30-minute call Thursday to lock cadence and sign-off path.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Security_Exhibit_v0.9.docx (docx)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: enforce minimal exposure + narrow inspection language

Quick internal thoughts (do not forward without edit):

- Agree with 3-tier cadence. Legal will push back on anything implying unlimited inspection rights — make clear "timeboxed, scoped, read-only, audited" in the exhibit.
- Limit log retention requests: provide 90-day window for full logs; anything older to be handled via agreement (avoid open-ended retention obligations).
- Pen-test: call out that customer-operated testing against shared infra is disallowed; allow customer-provided scope and independent 3rd-party testers only if run in a supplier-managed lab or dedicated staging with identical baseline. For production pen-tests, require a single supplier point-of-contact and an approval checklist (change freeze, rollbacks, MQA runbook).
- Evidence packaging: prefer weekly digest bundles for "scoped sample" requests (max 3 bundles in a 30-day period). This keeps ops load bounded.

I can draft redlines to the exhibit that translate these bullets into contract language. Marcus — can you confirm if the 90-day log export is feasible for all regions (we may need to note EU-specific constraints)?

Karthik

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@medtechco.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit — evidence handoff path and inspection windows (proposed final)

Sarah — following internal review, we can commit to the following as Exhibit language (summary):

1) Evidence cadence: quarterly SOC 2 Type II + ability to request scoped sample bundles (weekly digest; up to 3 per 30 days) for production-tagged resources.
2) Sampling bands: define the three tiers (Light / Scoped sample / Full inspection) with explicit limits: read-only exports, redaction rules for PII, and maximum 14-day supplier-coordinated full inspections.
3) Logs & retention: standard delivery is 90 days of logs; any longer retention or forensic requests require a separate data retrieval agreement and cost estimate.
4) Pen-test: customer-run tests against shared systems are not allowed. Customer may engage third-party testers if tests occur in supplier-managed staging or in a supplier-coordinated production window with pre-approval and an ops checklist (change freeze, runbook, rollback test).

Action items:
- Sarah / Rajiv: confirm you’re ok with weekly digest bundles for scoped sampling and the 90-day baseline.
- Redwood (Karthik): produce contract redlines that convert bullets into exhibit language (target by COB Fri).
- Neha: set up DocuSign link for exhibit once final redlines agreed.

I’ve attached the pen-test scope proposal we discussed. If OK, let’s schedule the call to finalize language.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: PenTest_Scope_Proposal.xlsx (xlsx)

Neha / team — thanks for the clear summary. Quick confirmations from MedTechCo: we accept the 90-day log baseline and the weekly digest model for scoped samples. The full-inspection 14-day limit is acceptable provided we get a 10-business-day notice for scheduling and the supplier POC is available.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood attach a simple signature exhibit (DocuSign) once Karthik posts redlines? We prefer a standalone exhibit to attach to the order form.
- On redaction: we’ll need a short example of how PII is redacted from the sample bundles (masking pattern) before legal will sign off.

We can do the call Friday at 11:00 PT if that works for your team. Sarah and I will join.

Thanks,
Rajiv Patel
Senior Security Engineer
MedTechCo
